creativity.reason: Level 2: the core business is chip design (multimedia ICs are not creative work), so only small current arts activities count: a sponsored art installation in Nanzhou and a student writing competition.

community.reason: Level 3: several named external education and community programs report participants and dollars (NT$100 million+ to universities, STEM Program reaching 2,673 students, NT$3 million Nanzhou plan), but they are not shown to be central to strategy, so level 4 is not reached.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 2: specific current inclusion activities (Global Family and Women in Tek resource groups, visually impaired therapists, Girls! TECH Action), with no membership figures and only small participant counts.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 2: the Genius at Home Impact Accelerator Program gives teams free executive mentorship to scale their ventures, with limited reach (132 proposals); the chip business itself does not enable founders.

ai.notes: Genius at Home changed in 2025 from a competition into an Impact Accelerator Program; it is scored as currently operating. For the 1+1 Science Connection program, participant figures for the 2025–2026 academic year are stated as 'anticipated' (planned), so only the accepted program and school counts are used. Community was considered for level 4 given NT$1.5 billion of cumulative university investment, but the filing ties much of this spending to the company's own R&D and talent pipeline, so the lower level was chosen. Nanzhou plan figures (NT$3 million, 38,461 participants) cover the whole plan, not just the arts pillar, so Creativity stays at 2. Workforce demographics (18.4% female) are disclosure only and were not scored. The employee children's scholarship (NT$9.338 million) is an employee benefit and was not counted as external education. The report refers to a separate sustainability report but itself describes specific activities, so coverage is sufficient on every theme and no second look is triggered.
